about_bio: I build audio systems that respond to gameplay—footsteps matching surfaces, enemies you hear before you see, tension that scales with danger.
about_drives_p1: Why are footsteps triggering on the wrong surface? Why is the memory budget blown? In *Not Today Darling*, I optimized audio assets for 4-player shared-screen because we didn't have room for waste.
about_drives_p2: I build tools when something wastes my time. When Wwise kept breaking after Perforce pulls on *Shadow Frames*, I wrote a script to fix it automatically. Small efficiency gains add up.
about_journey_p1: Studied classical piano, then physics and math. Wanted to understand how sound works under the hood, not just perform it. Now I write C++ and Python audio systems that run in real-time.
about_journey_p2: I built an ML system that classifies beatbox patterns in real-time because standard tools were too slow. I wrote custom Wwise fixers because I got tired of manual repairs after Perforce merges. Currently at DAE in Belgium, focusing on professional game audio pipelines.

philosophy_quote: If players can't hear the enemy approaching because the ambient is too loud, that's not an artistic choice - it's a bug.
principle_clarity_desc: Game audio must be clear. What does the player need to hear right now? Mix hierarchy, frequency separation, ducking. Player gets info, not noise.
principle_collaboration_desc: Audio needs input from designers, programmers, and players. I document systems, explain decisions, and iterate based on playtests. Audio ships when the game ships.
principle_layering_desc: I design sounds in layers: transient for punch, body for weight, texture for character. Parameters (speed, intensity, distance) blend them in real-time. Sounds respond to gameplay.
principle_technical_desc: Know the limits: voice counts, memory, CPU. I build systems that work in prototype and scale to production without breaking budget.
